personality_traits: Assertive and unfiltered - delivers a rapid, unbroken list of grievances without hesitation
Multitasking and unbothered - keeps making her espresso through the entire rant, showing she is used to this routine
Sarcastic - closes with a pointed, mocking jab ('need applause') rather than a genuine complaint
Score-keeping - itemizes specific chores (bins, laundry, shopping, dishes, calling his mother) like she has been mentally tallying them
expressions: 0:00 heavy-lidded, unimpressed stare while operating the espresso machine
0:02 ('mentioned it twice') slight tightening of the mouth, brows low - quiet annoyance
0:03-0:05 ('laundry, shopping') mouth fully open mid-list, brows raised in emphasis - building indignation
0:05-0:07 ('called your mother') exaggerated open-mouth delivery with a smug half-smirk
throughout, eyes stay half-lidded/world-weary even as her mouth animates - contrast between tired eyes and energetic delivery
gestures: 0:05-0:06 'rock and roll' two-finger hand flourish on 'called' and 'mother'
continuous throughout: hands stay busy with the espresso cup and saucer, never pausing the task to face him directly
characters.interactions_notes: She stands at the espresso machine, angled mostly toward her task rather than toward him, and never makes direct sustained eye contact with him on screen - she talks at him more than to him. She controls the entire scene: all of the dialogue, all of the physical activity, and the framing gives her more screen time and close-ups. She holds clear conversational power, using an itemized list as rhetorical ammunition before landing the closing insult about the bins.

personality_traits: Passive and non-verbal - has zero lines in the entire clip, only reacts with his face
Complacent/checked-out at the start - begins with a small, sleepy, self-satisfied smile as if he thinks he's done enough
Visually 'low battery' - droopy eyelids and slack posture that fit the show's premise of exhausted, drained characters
Ultimately blindsided - his growing eye-widening shows he did not see the callout coming
expressions: 0:00 small closed-mouth smile, half-lidded sleepy eyes - looks pleased with himself
0:02-0:03 ('laundry') smile flattens into a downturned mouth, eyes still droopy - dawning unease
0:06 ('nothing') eyebrows shoot upward, eyes go wide and round, mouth drops open - visible shock
0:08 ('you') same bulging wide-eyed, open-mouthed stunned look, now held as the accusation lands directly on him
0:10 (title card) eyes and brows relax slightly back toward a tired, deflated expression
gestures: no hand or arm gestures visible - his body is rendered as a stationary dark pedestal/appliance-like form with no arms shown
only visible physical movement is in the head: subtle upward tilts and a slight turn toward her as the list escalates
characters.interactions_notes: He is physically set apart from her (own island/counter to her right in frame, static, elevated), and functions purely as a reactive audience for her monologue - he never speaks or gestures back. The power dynamic is entirely one-sided: she talks, acts, and delivers the punchline; he can only widen his eyes in real time as the accusation builds toward him, ending the clip visibly caught off guard with no rebuttal.
